SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WATER ITS RESOURCES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Water its resources helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT WATER
We use water for drinking, cooking, cleaning, and farming.
Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.
Unsafe water can cause disease — store drinking water in clean covered containers.

PART 1: Construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering

What this means
In this part you learn to construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Water its resources” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Water its resources is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Conserve water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water for plants where safe.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Water its resources” around your school. (skill: construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Water its resources to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Water its resources from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Water its resources: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Water its resources?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Water its resources means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: construct a simple water dirty water and discuss how the filter for cleaning water at water could be made clean and home safe for use (decantation, filtering.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
